An AI-driven development methodology whe: An AI-driven development methodology where multiple specialist agents handle the whole lifecycle — from planning to operation — through defined stages. Unlike plain AI coding, every decision has a human approval gate.
It prevents the lost context, vanished r: It prevents the lost context, vanished rationale, and silent failures that appear as a project grows, using per-stage ownership, gate verification, and an audit log.
It starts with Initialization (automatic: It starts with Initialization (automatic), then proceeds through Ideation, Inception, Construction, and Operation. There is a verification gate between phases.
The flow chart is a <b>catalog of possib: The flow chart is a catalog of possible stages. A project is not run through all 32 stages at once; it is split by intent and executed iteratively.
Every stage except Initialization will n: Every stage except Initialization will not move on without human approval.
Even if the code disappears, the rationa: Even if the code disappears, the rationale and artifacts remain. History is traced through the audit log.
When a human corrects a result, that cor: When a human corrects a result, that correction is accumulated as a permanent rule in Space memory.
The first intent establishes the archite: The first intent establishes the architecture; later intents get progressively faster as accumulated Space memory lets conditional stages auto-skip.
Decides which stages run and how deep: Decides which stages run and how deep
Scope decides which stages run in an int: Scope decides which stages run in an intent, and how deeply. Set it with /aidlc --scope <name>; if omitted it is auto-detected.
All stages — for establishing the founda: All stages — for establishing the foundation
If a stock scope does not fit, use <code: If a stock scope does not fit, use /aidlc compose "<task>" to get an EXECUTE/SKIP grid proposal, then run it after approval.
Use <code>/aidlc --depth minimal|standar: Use /aidlc --depth minimal|standard|comprehensive to adjust the detail of documents and questions.
Use <code>/aidlc --test-strategy &lt;lev: Use /aidlc --test-strategy <level> to control test coverage separately.
Start by describing what to build after: Start by describing what to build after /aidlc, or with /aidlc --scope feature.
At the end of each stage, choose approve: At the end of each stage, choose approve/revise/reject. The [Answer]: tags in the questions file are the source of truth.
Jump to a stage with <code>/aidlc --stag: Jump to a stage with /aidlc --stage <slug>, to a phase with /aidlc --phase <name>. Add --single to run it standalone.
Use the park button in the Actions view,: Use the park button in the Actions view, or park/unpark. Artifacts are version-controlled under aidlc/spaces/<space>/intents/<intent>/.
